text:
liam: heads-up — noticing a cluster-level uptick in preemptible evictions from the us-west2 spot pool over the last 6 hours. about ~6% of active streams are being cut mid-token and clients see truncated responses. thinking we should add a streaming cutover + lightweight checkpointing handshake to avoid partial outputs and double charges. thoughts? :thinking:

maya: can you paste an example of the failure pattern? is it always mid-token or sometimes during kv-cache writes?

liam: mostly mid-token while the runtime is flushing to local disk. stack traces show gRPC stream aborted + SIGTERM within ~8s of eviction notice. not enough time to flush large KV pages. logs: `runtime: evict signal received, remaining ttl=7s` then `stream aborted: io: read/write on closed pipe`.

jon: we hit this a few weeks back in eu-central with similar behavior. proposal that worked: 1) emit a small checkpoint containing (stream_id, last_token_index, idempotency_token) to shared metadata store, 2) return a cutover frame to client with reattach info, 3) requeue unfinished request to on-demand pool (or warm on-demand slot) with a short TTL. avoids double-generation and gives clients deterministic resume.

kevin: agree but caveat: checkpointing full KV to s3 on every eviction is heavy. prefer a tiny summary checkpoint + keep the large KV in a hot cache like local-ssd snapshotting only the changed pages. we can also compress diffs. cost tradeoff is small compared to re-generating 200 tokens on a high-qps model.

liam: exactly. rough sketch of handshake payload I had in mind:

```
{ "stream_id": "s-123", "last_token": 342, "idempotency": "uuid-xxx", "resume_endpoint": "runtimes-west2/attach?s=s-123&t=uuid-xxx" }
```

Client receives a `CUTOVER` frame with that payload and stops waiting. we mark request as `paused` in orchestrator and attempt fast requeue to non-spot or dedicated pool if capacity available. if requeue fails within TTL (default 30s) we return a graceful partial response with a `partial=true` flag and link to resume info.

maya: default TTL 30s seems fine but let's make it overrideable per-customer/request. high-SLA customers might want 120s and forced fallback to dedicated. also need to ensure billing is idempotent — if client reconnects and we re-run some tokens, we shouldn't bill twice.

jon: idempotency can be achieved by coupling `idempotency` + `last_token` + server-side dedupe window. if a requeued run has the same idempotency token we do a cheap validation: compare generated_prefix_hash with checkpointed prefix. if match, we resume from last_token rather than re-gen.

kevin: operational concerns: 1) support in our gRPC streaming layer to pause and reattach 2) world-visible metadata store (etcd?) that survives node eviction 3) backpressure so we don't overload on-demand pool during evict storms.

sre-oncall: +1 on backpressure. we should have a token-bucket per-customer to limit requeue rate into on-demand, and a global circuit that flips to best-effort when on-demand usage spiking. also expose metrics: `evict_cutovers`, `cutover_requeues`, `cutover_resume_success` for alerting.

liam: agree on metrics. also thinking about mixed-capacity pools: make routing policy prefer spot until a cutover rate > X% or requeue queue depth > Y, then fall back automatically to reserved capacity for that customer-route. e.g., route policy: `if cutover_rate > 2% and requeue_fail_rate > 5% => migrate 10% of traffic to dedicated`.

maya: canary plan: roll the handshake to 5% of traffic, watch `partial_responses` and `bill_discrepancies`. Add a debug header for clients: `X-Cutover-Debug: 1` to surface resume tokens in logs for the first few customers.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout plan for `streaming-cutover` feature submitted by liam. target: eng-sre-canary namespace, 5% traffic, start: 1719005400.

jon: one more edge-case: network partition between compute node and metadata store during eviction. need local fallback where node persists checkpoint to local-ssd and exposes it via ephemeral reattach endpoint (node-proxy) while orchestrator tries to copy to global store. node-proxy should be gated behind a short TTL (e.g., 60s) and require mutual auth.

kevin: agree. we should also implement a cheap verification step on resume: before resuming expensive decoding, run a `verify_prefix` that checks first N tokens against client's prefix hash to ensure no divergence — cheap and prevents wasting GPU cycles.

liam: good point. I'll draft an RFC with: handshake spec, checkpoint schema, requeue policy, TTL knobs, billing idempotency, metrics, and canary rollout steps. target PR by EOD tomorrow.

maya: please include config example for route policy and the requeue token-bucket defaults.

liam: will do. quick config draft in thread:

```
route_policies:
  - name: spot-preferred
    cutover_threshold: 0.02  # fraction
    requeue_depth_threshold: 50
    fallback_percent: 0.10
requeue:
  default_ttl_seconds: 30
  max_ttl_seconds: 120
  per_customer_token_bucket_rate: 5/s
```

sre-oncall: thumbs up. let's sync 30m after the RFC PR. also flagging potential perf test: simulate 20% eviction surge and verify resume success > 95% and additional cost < 7% compared to full dedicated fallback. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

liam: thanks — filing RFC now. tagging @maya @jon for review. :rocket:
